bodies.classification: Terrestrial Planetary Satellite / Airless Basaltic & Highland Body
bodies.surface_pressure_note: Not Available (Ultra-high vacuum regime < 10^-12 hPa; no bulk atmosphere)
bodies.liquid_water_note: Not Available (Liquid water thermodynamically unstable at surface vacuum; sequestered as cryogenic solid volatile ice in PSRs)
bodies.radiation_regime: Unattenuated galactic cosmic rays (GCR) and solar particle events (SPE)

targets.name: Lunar South Pole: Shackleton Crater Rim

geology.stratigraphy: Pre-Nectarian / Nectarian impact basin ejecta (South Pole-Aitken basin margin) overlain by Shackleton impact structure (~3.6 Ga)
dominant_minerals: Cryogenic Volatile Water Ice (H2O / OH) in Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs)
geomorphic_features: Sharp crater rim crest (21 km diameter)
Steep inner wall slopes (>30 degrees) subject to mass wasting
Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs) receiving zero direct sunlight for billions of years
Adjacent Connecting Ridge exhibiting high seasonal illumination (>86% sunlight)

key_scientific_questions: What is the concentration, isotopic signature, and physical form of volatile ice trapped within the PSR?
How does regolith gardening by micrometeoroid impact affect volatile preservation?
How can astronaut habitats and mobility systems navigate 30-degree slopes in cryogenic shadowed conditions?

instruments.measurement: Precision topographic elevation, slope, RMS roughness (5-20 m/px)
9-channel infrared surface brightness temperature (50-400 K) and thermal inertia
Radar circular polarization ratio (CPR) and 0.43-3.0 um NIR water-ice absorption bands

data_confidence.confidence_notes: Orbital laser altimetry and thermal radiometry are exceptionally high resolution; subsurface ice distribution and in-situ mineralogy await direct surface verification by Artemis astronauts.

targets.name: Lunar South Pole: Malapert Mountain (Plateau)

geology.stratigraphy: Massive South Pole-Aitken (SPA) basin rim mountain block elevated over 5 km
geomorphic_features: High solar illumination peak (>89% summer sunlight)
Continuous direct line-of-sight to Earth for deep space communications
Moderate summit slopes (5-15 deg) favorable for landing architecture

key_scientific_questions: Does the summit expose primordial crust from the pre-Nectarian South Pole-Aitken impact event?
Is Malapert optimal as an astronomical lunar far-side radio observatory and communications relay node?

instruments.measurement: High-resolution topographic relief and slope maps
Day/night thermal profiles and rock abundance mapping

data_confidence.confidence_notes: Well mapped by LRO orbital instruments; lack of in-situ sampling limits petrological certainty.

bodies.classification: Terrestrial Silicate Planet with Thin CO2 Atmosphere
bodies.surface_pressure_note: Mean 6.1 hPa (610 Pa); ranges seasonally from 5.8 to 7.5 hPa due to polar CO2 cap condensation/sublimation
bodies.liquid_water_note: Not Available at present day surface (below triple point in most regimes; transient metastable brines hypothesized)
bodies.radiation_regime: High solar UV-A, UV-B, UV-C (unshielded by thin CO2 column; no ozone layer); galactic cosmic rays

targets.name: Jezero Crater: Western Fan & Delta

geology.stratigraphy: Late Noachian / Early Hesperian lacustrine delta deposits prograding into an open-basin impact lake (~3.7 Ga)
geomorphic_features: Classic curved deltaic distributary channel networks
Prominent erosional delta scarp (~60 m high)
Eolian transverse aeolian ridges (TARs) and sand ripples

key_scientific_questions: Are organic biosignatures preserved in the fine-grained clay and carbonate-rich mudstones?
What was the duration, chemistry, and habitability of the Jezero paleolake during the Noachian-Hesperian transition?
How do return-sample cores selected by Perseverance represent early Martian aqueous environments?

instruments.measurement: Global elevation, crater basin depth, regional slopes

instruments.instrument: NASA CRISM (Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars)
instruments.measurement: Hyperspectral VNIR identification of smectites, carbonates, and hydrated silica (18 m/px)

instruments.instrument: NASA HiRISE (High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment)
instruments.measurement: 0.25 m/px optical imaging showing strata layers and boulders
Thermal inertia mapping (100 m/px) discriminating bedrock from sand dunes
PIXL (micro-XRF), SHERLOC (deep-UV Raman), SuperCam (LIBS & VISIR), RIMFAX (radar)

data_confidence.confidence_notes: Exceptionally high confidence due to combination of multi-spacecraft orbital sensors and active in-situ rover ground-truth.

targets.name: Jezero Crater: Séítah Formation (Crater Floor)

geology.stratigraphy: Early igneous unit forming the basement floor of Jezero Crater, subsequently modified by aqueous alteration
dominant_minerals: Secondary Halite & Sulfate salts in vugs

key_scientific_questions: Was the Séítah formation formed as a thick lava lake cumulate or a sub-volcanic layered mafic intrusion?
What do the carbonate alteration coatings reveal about early Martian groundwater and atmospheric CO2 sequestration?

instruments.instrument: Mars 2020 PIXL (Planetary Instrument for X-ray Lithochemistry)
instruments.measurement: Elemental micro-mapping (<120 um) verifying olivine cumulate petrology
Orbital olivine absorption band at 1.0 um and high-res outcrop mapping

data_confidence.confidence_notes: In-situ abrasion patches and sample cores (e.g., 'Dourbes' and 'Robine') have verified cumulate olivine petrology.
